formation.explanation: Append is proposal admission: followers forward or buffer, leaders buffer in Prepare or append in Accept. A new leader gathers sender-indexed promises, selects the maximum accepted history and maximum reported decision index, synchronizes storage, then sends AcceptSync. Followers acknowledge synchronized or appended log indices. The leader counts per-sender accepted indices for its ballot and advances decisions when the configured write quorum supports an index. Decide/AcceptDecide propagate the index; public reads distinguish Decided from Undecided and applications consume the former. InternalStorage read classifies values below the decided index; the actor has a separate proposal-identity assignment and completion layer, so correct decided-index advancement alone does not establish correct append_notify completion.

context.explanation: BLE uses heartbeat rounds and configuration-tagged ballots to select leadership. SequencePaxos independently requires a ballot higher than its existing leader and promise. A local leader resets volatile quorum accounting and persists its promise; a receiving follower persists a higher promise and enters Prepare. Accept processing requires the promised ballot and appropriate phase, and ordered messages use session/counter sequence numbers. Older requests are rejected or ignored; higher unexpected accepts and sequence gaps initiate recovery. Persisted promises start recovery after reconstruction. NotAccepted marks a peer as having promised higher. Build derives peers from configuration, passes quorum policy to both core components, reloads stored promise into BLE and reconstructs cached log metadata. The actor serializes protocol dispatch but can dispatch multiple incoming messages between ticks.

connection.explanation: Authority is insufficient without prepare support: prior accepted rounds and lengths determine the history installed in the new ballot, while prior decisions constrain the reported decision prefix. Buffered proposals are incorporated after history selection unless a StopSign is present; follower synchronization forwards buffered proposals if not stopped. Old-ballot acknowledgments cannot advance a new leader because accepted handlers require matching ballots and leader state is reset. Recovery reuses equal-ballot Prepare only in Recover and starts a new accept sequence session. StopSign travels with synchronized history and stops new local admission; starting the next configuration and carrying application history is a documented caller duty. Storage reconstruction supplies prior promise/history; runtime notification bookkeeping remains volatile and separate. Assigned position is consumed with a later decided-boundary read; its ballot is checked only after the success branch, leaving entry identity across replacement as a specific question.
